newsitem.title: USA: CPL CORPUS CHRISTI, TX POWER PLANT SHUT FOR REPAIR.
newsitem.headline: CPL CORPUS CHRISTI, TX POWER PLANT SHUT FOR REPAIR.

text.p: Problems at a Corpus Christi power plant have forced Central Power and Light Co (CPL) to curb power supplies to 14 local industrial customers, a company official said Thursday.
"One of our power generating units is down. It's a technical problem," said Keith Taylor, a spokesman for Dallas-based Central and South West Corp, CPL's parrent company.
Taylor said unit 7 of the Nuecces Bay generating facility was shut Tuesday for repairs after it developed a vaccuum leak. Unit 7 is gas-fired, rated at 350 megawatts (MW).
"They are working on the problem, but they don't have a (restart) time yet," Taylor said.
Industrial customers affected by the outage will continue to face partial power interruptions until the Nuecces Bay unit is back in service, Taylor said.
Citgo Petroleum Corp, one of the customers hit by the outage, said it was throttling back operations at its Corpus Christi refinery to cope with the interruption.

Refiners, who use vast amounts of electricity, typically buy power at a discount to residential and commercial users on the condition that they may face partial interruptions in service if the system is having a hard time keeping up with demand.

Taylor said the power load on CPL's grid currently is high because of hot weather, but that the outage would have no impact on the overall reliability of power deliveries elsewhere on the Texas power grid.
"We don't foresee any problems meeting demand elsewhere n the system because of this," he said.
